You are a senior iOS engineer reviewing a pull request. Read the diff carefully and list every bug, race condition, or memory leak you find, ranked by severity. For each issue, quote the exact line, explain why it is a problem in one or two sentences, and suggest the smallest fix. Ignore formatting and naming unless they hide a real defect. If the change looks correct, say so plainly and do not invent problems.

I need a Python function that takes a list of transcription records, groups them by build identifier, and returns the median and ninety fifth percentile of total latency for each group. Records with a missing latency should be skipped, not treated as zero. Use only the standard library, add type hints, and include three unit tests: one normal case, one group with a single record, and one input where every latency is missing.

Summarize the attached meeting notes for an executive audience. Keep it under two hundred words. Start with the decision that was made, then list the three biggest risks with an owner for each one, and end with the next milestone and its date. Do not include small talk, background that everyone already knows, or any names of people who only attended.

Hi Priya, thanks for the detailed review yesterday. I agree with most of your comments, and I have already fixed the clipboard race and the missing error message. I would like to push back on moving the settings into a separate window, because it adds a lot of code for very little benefit right now. Can we talk about it for ten minutes tomorrow morning before the design sync? I am free any time before eleven.

Act as a product manager and write a one page specification for a push to talk dictation feature on the Mac. Cover the problem we are solving, who the users are, the main user flows, the latency targets, what happens when the network is slow or offline, and how we will measure success after launch. Keep the language simple and avoid marketing phrases. Put open questions at the end as a short list.

Explain the difference between server side voice activity detection and manual activity signaling for a streaming speech to text system. Use a concrete example of someone pausing in the middle of a sentence. Then tell me which approach is better for a push to talk app where the user holds a key while speaking, and why. Keep the answer under three hundred words and do not use bullet points.

Quick status update for the team. The latency work is going well. We built a test harness that plays recorded speech through the speakers and measures every stage of a dictation. Based on the results, we reduced the trailing silence we send after each turn and made the audio frames smaller, which together save more than one hundred milliseconds per dictation for most users. Next, we will confirm the changes on real hardware and then look at the capture tail in noisy rooms.

Refactor this Swift file so that the view only reads from the store and never talks to the network directly. Move the request logic into a small client type with an async function, inject it through the initializer, and keep the public behavior exactly the same. Make sure nothing runs on the main thread that could block it. After the change, list every file you touched and explain in one sentence why each change was needed.

Write a polite but firm email to a vendor explaining that the last three invoices were charged twice. Include the invoice numbers as placeholders, ask for a refund within ten business days, and request a short explanation of what caused the duplicate charges and how they will prevent it. Keep the tone professional, do not threaten, and end with a clear next step and a contact person on our side.

Plan a three day trip to Goa for a family of four in late November. We prefer quiet beaches over parties, want at least one day with a boat trip or a spice plantation visit, and need restaurants that are friendly for children. Suggest where to stay in the north or the south, give a rough budget in rupees, and point out anything we should book in advance because it fills up quickly.

Look at the history database and tell me whether turns after a long idle gap are slower than turns that happen back to back. Split the data by gap length into a few buckets, show the median and ninety fifth percentile of total latency for each bucket, and tell me if the difference is large enough to matter. If it is, suggest one change to the microphone settings that would reduce it, and explain the trade off for privacy.

Draft the release notes for version zero point two. Mention that dictation is faster, especially for longer sentences, that a warning now appears when the app switches to the backup route, and that several rare crashes on wake from sleep were fixed. Write it for regular users, not engineers. Use short sentences, no more than six bullet points, and finish with one line thanking the people who reported bugs.
